sents.t: When we got back to Oakville, Lily and I organized a donation drive for the families who were affected by the hurricane.
Collection boxes were placed at Oakville Books, Maple Café, and Danny’s bank.
In just two weeks, more than three thousand pounds of food, water, and clothes were collected.
Mrs. Johnson let us use the food bank warehouse, and everything was sorted by volunteers in the evenings.
A trucking company offered to drive the boxes to Louisiana for free.
A reporter from the Oakville Times called me.
“We’ve heard about your donation drive. Can we interview you?”
The next day, a photographer took a picture of Lily and me in front of the truck.
I was asked how the idea had started, and I told her about the waiter who said, “You learn to respect the storm.”
On Sunday morning, Rosa knocked on my door, waving the newspaper.
Our photo was printed on the front page under the headline “Oakville Helps the Gulf Coast.”
One was framed and hung on the wall of Maple Café.
Another was mailed to my mom.
“One small idea can be heard very far away.”
